recommendations.body: `_ClaudeInvokeRunnerObserver` in `plan_tool/shell.py` claims "the runner tells a bare writer apart from a caller-built observer by `isinstance(run_logger, RunLogWriter)`" and that `run`'s call sites get interrupt richness "via its own adapter" from "a later step" — neither is true at HEAD: `plan_tool/backend_runner.py` has no `isinstance(run_logger, RunLogWriter)` check anywhere (confirmed by grep), and `run`'s bare writer (passed unchanged from `launcher.py:shell_invoker` through `_run_streaming_once`) already receives `run_interrupted` from the runner's own uniformly-widened fallback, not from a separate adapter in `launcher.py`. The matching claim in `plan_tool/run_log.py:RunnerObserver`'s docstring ("only a purpose-built observer... gets its `run_interrupted` calls forwarded for real — a bare writer's internal fallback leaves interrupt handling to a later step") is the same stale statement restated. A reader trusting either docstring could "restore" a distinction that was deliberately removed, regressing the tested behavior.
recommendations.suggested_action: rewrite `_ClaudeInvokeRunnerObserver`'s docstring in `plan_tool/shell.py` and `RunnerObserver`'s docstring in `plan_tool/run_log.py` to state that both a bare `RunLogWriter` and a caller-built observer now receive `run_interrupted` uniformly, with no `isinstance` gate
